publicReleaseNotes: Cron D1 reads stay flat as incidents accumulate. Cron used to scan every alert contact schedule row and every outbox row of a monitor on each run, so reads grew with every incident ever opened. On a fixture with 0, 50 and 500 past incidents, a Cron run read 186, 6,092 and 508,742 D1 rows before, and 190, 191 and 191 after (F6). Finished schedules keep their rows as history. A late kick no longer re-probes every monitor: a console check that fills a Cron minute that never arrived, late in its minute, no longer leaves the next Cron probe 12 seconds behind it (F5). A Cron delivered up to 30 seconds early still probes, waiting for its minute instead of skipping it (F7). When upgrading from 0.5.31, 0098_bound_contact_schedule_reads.sql adds four indexes on alert contact schedules and the outbox. Earlier migrations are byte-identical. The @runeditrun/rer pin stays at 0.2.131. The backup and upgrade guidance under 0.5.26 still applies.
